saints.name: St. Anastasius I
saints.title: Pope
saints.shortBlurb: A pope praised by Jerome for his holiness, who condemned the errors drawn from the writings of Origen…
biography: A Roman by birth, the son of Maximus, Anastasius succeeded Siricius as bishop of Rome in 399 and reigned little more than two years. Brief as his pontificate was, he was esteemed for his poverty of life and apostolic zeal; Jerome, who knew him, praised the holiness of his rule.

His days fell in the first Origenist controversy. Moved by the pleas of Theophilus of Alexandria, he formally condemned the errors drawn from Origen's writings, and when Rufinus of Aquileia sent him an apology for his translation of Origen, the pope, writing to John of Jerusalem in 401, made no secret of his distrust.

He died on 19 December 401 and was buried in the cemetery of Pontian on the Via Portuensis, where his tomb was found in later ages near that of his successor Innocent I — said by the Liber Pontificalis to have been his son, born before his ordination. His feast is kept on the day of his death.
saints.knownFor: Condemning Origenism and his repute for holiness among the Fathers.

sources.text: The Roman Martyrology (1914 English ed.; public domain)
